chunk_findings.detail: The new guard rejects non-dict tables except `None`, and it does not validate the values inside those tables. A store file containing `{"format": STORE_VERSION, "tokens": null, "pairings": {}}` passes `_read`, then `tokens_list` calls `AU.disagreements`, which does `stored = _read(...)["tokens"]` and `set(stored)`, raising `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable`. Similarly, `{"format": STORE_VERSION, "tokens": {"abc": null}, "pairings": {}}` passes `_read`, and when the id is not in the logged rows, `disagreements` does `row["name"]` on `None` and crashes. Thus wrong-typed store fields can still crash instead of being refused.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/auth.py:_read

chunk_findings.detail: `disagreements` compares only token ids against the `logged` rows it is given, but `tokens_list` passes the already-active-only rows unless `--all` is used. If the log has an expired or revoked row for a token while the store still contains that token id (expired store rows are not necessarily pruned), default `tokens list` omits that log row from `by_id`; the first loop then emits “is live in the store but has no log record,” even though the log does have a record and the token may not be live. The note should compare against all log rows or check state/expiry, not just presence in the active row list.

chunk_findings.detail: A store `verify` refuses is treated as “no disagreement”. `_read` raises `AuthRefused` for a bad format, an unreadable file, or (after this change) a non-dict `tokens`/`pairings` table, and `disagreements` catches that and returns `[]`. Given `{"format": 1, "tokens": []}` (or any unreadable store) and a log that still lists an active token, `tokens list` stays silent while every `verify` refuses, which is the lie this note was added to stop.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/auth.py:disagreements

chunk_findings.detail: `null` and bad rows still pass the new guard. A dict table with a non-dict row (`{"format": 1, "tokens": {"abc": null}}`) also passes `_read`; `tokens list` now calls `disagreements`, which does `row['name']` and turns a previously log-only command into a `TypeError`/`KeyError`.

chunk_findings.detail: The second loop treats a token id merely being present in `stored` as a live store row. If the store still contains an expired row while the log row is `ACTIVE`, `token_id in stored` causes `continue`, so no disagreement note is emitted. Because expiry is held twice (epoch in the store, ISO in the log) and can disagree, a valid-looking state such as store `expires = now - 1` and log `expires_at = now + 1` makes `rows()` return the log row as active, `disagreements` see the id in `stored`, and return no note; `tokens list` then shows the token active with no warning even though `verify` will refuse it. The first loop already recognizes `expires <= now` as a row verify would refuse, so the second loop should test the stored row’s liveness/dict shape, not just key presence.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/auth.py:disagreements

chunk_findings.detail: `tokens_list` passes only active log rows to `disagreements` unless `--all` is used, but the first loop in `disagreements` uses `token_id in by_id` to decide that a log record exists. Given a token whose log row expired one second ago while the store row’s `expires` is still in the future (the dual-expiry skew), default `tokens list` omits the expired log row from `logged`, so the first loop emits “token … has no log record” even though `tokens list --all` would show an expired log record. The earlier probe about non-dict store rows does not address this active-only filtering; either pass all log rows for reconciliation or change the note to say “no active log record.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/auth.py:tokens_list

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_read` guard validates only that the top-level `tokens` and `pairings` tables are dicts; wrong-typed fields inside a dict row still reach the new liveness comparison. The previous refutation that non-dict rows are skipped does not cover wrong-typed values inside otherwise dict rows.

chunk_findings.detail: The new id-only reconciliation still lets a store/log expiry disagreement pass silently. The second loop suppresses the “log active, store ended” note whenever the token id exists in `stored`, even if that store row is expired and `verify` will refuse it. For example, with a store row `{"abc": {"name": "gw", "expires": CLOCK.wall() - 1}}` and a log row whose `state` is still `ACTIVE`, `tokens list` prints the token as active and emits no note, although verification fails; the previous probe’s “no longer reads store-row fields” is exactly why this disagreement can no longer be detected. The converse is also true after the `everything=True` change: if the log row is expired/not active while the store row is still live, default `tokens list` omits the token and `disagreements` emits no note because the id is present in `by_id`, even though `verify` accepts the token.

chunk_findings.detail: The refutation does not answer the earlier disagreement. `disagreements` still treats any store key as agreement: `if token_id in stored or row["state"] != ACTIVE: continue` never looks at whether that store row would still verify. Given store `expires` of `now - 1` and a log row `{id: "abc", name: "gw", state: ACTIVE, expires_at: now + 1}` (the dual-expiry skew this change was meant to surface), `rows(..., everything=True)` keeps the log row active, the id is in `stored`, and no note is emitted, while `verify` refuses the expired store row and `tokens list` still shows the token as active.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_read` validation only rejects the whole `tokens` or `pairings` table if it is not a dict; it still accepts malformed rows inside those tables. Given a store whose `format` is correct and whose `pairings` table is a dict, e.g. `{"format": STORE_VERSION, "pairings": {"ABC": {"salt": "s", "hash": "h", "attempts": "0"}}}`, `_read` returns successfully. In `_spend`, a pairing code that matches the id but fails the hash comparison then reaches `row["attempts"] += 1` and raises `TypeError` instead of the clear `AuthRefused` the change says wrong-typed store fields should produce.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/auth.py:_read

chunk_findings.detail: The failure this test injects is a `redeem` log-append failure after the store has already been written, so the new store row is a live token missing from the log. Verification reads the store, so that token will verify; the disagreement `tokens list` should report for this case is “unrecorded”/live-verify (or the store should be reconciled), not “will not verify”. The assertion `assert "will not verify" in out` is therefore wrong for the created disagreement: if `tokens list` correctly reports the redeem-created unrecorded token as verifying, the test fails; if it passes only because an unrelated ended/revoked token emits `will not verify`, the test does not actually assert the store-before-log disagreement it claims to cover.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_auth_tokens.py:test_tokens_list_names_a_store_and_log_disagreement
